title: MCFuser: High-Performance and Rapid Fusion of Memory-Bound Compute-Intensive Operators
problem: Operator fusion fails to extend to multiple compute-intensive operators due to saturated computation throughput. Generating optimal fused kernels is hindered by limited search spaces, redundant memory access, and prolonged tuning times.
motivation: Operator fusion improves data locality and alleviates GPU memory bandwidth pressure, which is critical for efficient GPU execution.
method: MCFuser fuses multiple compute-intensive operators (like matrix multiplies and convolutions) into a single GPU kernel by breaking the computation into tiles that fit in faster on-chip memory and analyzing the data flow to eliminate redundant memory reads. Rather than trying all possible kernel designs, it prunes bad options upfront and uses a mathematical model to predict performance, guided by heuristic search (smart, targeted search) to find an optimized kernel quickly.
key_novelty: The core idea is using tiling strategies combined with data-flow analysis to automatically combine multiple compute-intensive operations into a single GPU kernel, with mathematical performance prediction replacing exhaustive trial-and-error tuning.
contributions: Framework for generating high-performance fused kernels for memory-bound compute-intensive operator chains
High-level tiling expressions to delineate comprehensive search space for fusion strategies
DAG analysis technique to eliminate redundant memory accesses in operator fusion
Analytical performance model with heuristic search for rapid kernel optimization
limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed in abstract
primary_theme: operator fusion and kernel optimization for GPUs
